text.p: An earthquake shook India's border region with Nepal on Sunday but there were no reports of damage or injuries, officials said.
The Indian Meteorological Department said the earthquake measured 5.5 on the Richter scale and occurred at 2.17 p.m. (0847 GMT).
The quake's epicentre was located in the western part of Uttar Pradesh state near the border with Nepal, a department official said.
Earthquakes between four and five on the Richter scale are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in populated areas.
In 1993, a quake of 6.4 on the Richter scale devastated a large area of Maharashtra state in western India, killing more than 11,000 people, and leaving about 150,000 homeless.
